units.en: For non ⟦0⟧ special forces technology, see ⟦1⟧

Special forces doctrines introduced in ⟦0⟧ allow nations to further specialize usage of their special forces. With ⟦1⟧ enabled, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ each have two unique subdoctrine choices available. With ⟦5⟧ enabled, players have access to the ⟦6⟧ special forces and their two subdoctrines as well. Players must choose which special forces they wish to elevate (and which of the two playstyles available for each special forces type to lean into) using their limited amount of [[#Special Forces Branch Specialization|special forces branch specializations], which can unlock the second ⟦7⟧.

Grand Doctrines represent the overall doctrine of your special forces. They provide bonuses when unlocked, as well as unique milestones for each track once mastered. Only one Grand Doctrine can be enabled at a time.

Expanded Special Forces Special Forces Capacity Multiplier: +4.0% Special Forces Division training time: -20.0% Special forces are able to perform missions that ordinary soldiers can not. We need to expand the training programs to get more of our soldiers qualified.

Elite Special Forces Special Forces Supply Grace: +24.0 Hour(s) Special Forces: Organization: +10.0 Only the best of the best will become special forces. The soldiers that make it through the training will be stronger, faster and fight harder than anyone else.

Unlike for ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and ⟦2⟧, Special Forces tracks are not split into different categories. Each of the two tracks has access to all eight of the subdoctrines (as long as the required DLCs are enabled), with the exception that you cannot pick to fill both tracks with a subdoctrine from the same type of Special Forces. For example, players cannot pick both Elevate the Mountaineers for one track and Cold Weather Specialists for the other. Just as each track shares the same options, the options available are not impacted by the choice of grand doctrine either. ⟦3⟧ is used to unlock milestones within the subdoctrine, granting further bonuses. Each track gains ⟦4⟧ when certain units engage in action or at a reduced rate while training. If a subdoctrine is not selected, up to 200 ⟦5⟧ is held in reserve.

When a track as been mastered, it unlocks the grand doctrine milestone for the track. This holds true for Special Forces tracks too; even though they aren't unique functionally, they are still distinct. The left track of the two, which is unlocked first, has a different milestone than the right track, which is unlocked second.

Subdoctrines allow special forces to further specialize in different types of combat. Subdoctrines provide some bonuses when picked and additional bonuses are unlocked when enough ⟦0⟧ is accumulated in each Doctrine Track. Only one Subdoctrine can be enabled from each type of Special Forces at a time. Grand Doctrines do not affect which Subdoctrines are available.
Unlike other doctrine types, Special Forces doctrines determine both what they gain mastery from and how much experience they cost (and of what type) from the subdoctrine, not the doctrine track.
Cold Weather Specialists / Elevate the Mountaineers
This pair of subdoctrines require having researched the ⟦0⟧ technology before they are unlocked.
